questions.prompt: RMSE between sim [0,1,2,3] and real [0,1,2,7]. Precision 0.001.
A friction coefficient estimate 0.60 with standard error 0.05. Lower end of a +-3 sigma range. Precision 0.001.
Randomization ranges are chosen 10x wider than the identified uncertainty. Likely effect?
options: More precise policies, because the training covers every possible case.
No noticeable effect, since the policy only sees the real parameters.
Faster training, because the policy can ignore any single example.
A conservative or infeasible policy, because it must work in unrealistic worlds.
questions.explanation: Too wide trades performance for coverage.

questions.prompt: Why run a mock hardware-in-the-loop stage before the tethered robot?
options: It exposes driver timing, delay and interface errors with no physical risk.
It removes the need for later tests on the tethered robot.
It is cheaper than simulation, as no model of the plant is needed.
It proves that the controller is optimal for the real plant.

questions.prompt: A controller is stable in sim with d=1 delay and unstable on hardware at the same gain. First suspect?
options: A wrong gravity constant in the simulator that also acts on hardware.
Additional delay in the real stack beyond the margin.
A different random seed used in the hardware run.
A slightly different link colour between simulation and hardware.
questions.explanation: Delay can destabilize without any parameter being wrong.

questions.prompt: Describe how to measure end-to-end delay of a real control loop and feed it into the simulator.
rubric: Uses timestamps or a loopback test to measure sensor-to-actuator delay with its distribution.
Adds the measured delay (in samples) and jitter to the simulator.
Compares simulated and real step responses and checks the margin.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Compare identification, domain randomization and real fine-tuning for closing a friction gap. Which would you try first and why?
rubric: States cost, safety and coverage of each strategy.
Chooses identification first with randomization around its uncertainty, fine-tuning last.
Names how to validate that the gap shrank (held-out parameters, hardware metric).
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Which result is the strongest evidence that a sim2real gap has narrowed?
options: A lower training reward in simulation after the parameters were updated.
Held-out hardware trajectories whose RMSE against simulation meets a pre-set gate, with worst cases reported.
A longer simulation horizon with the same parameters as before.
A smooth-looking video of one successful run on the real robot.
questions.explanation: Pre-registered limits, held-out data and worst cases.
